'''Didier Astruc''' (born 9 June 1946 in [[Versailles (city)|Versailles]]) carried out his studies in chemistry in [[Rennes]]. After a Ph.D. with professor R. Dabard in [[organometallic chemistry]], he did post-doctoral studies with professor [[Richard R. Schrock|R. R. Schrock]] (2005 [[Nobel Prize in Chemistry|Nobel Laureate]]) at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] Cambridge, Massachusetts, in the [[United States|U.S.]] and later a sabbatical year with professor K. P. C. Vollhardt<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://chem.berkeley.edu/faculty/vollhardt/index.php|title=Faculty & Research &#124; College of Chemistry}}</ref> at [[University of California at Berkeley|the University of California at Berkeley]]. He became a [[CNRS]] Director of research in Rennes, then in 1983 full Professor of Chemistry at the University Bordeaux 1. He is known for his work on [[electron-reservoir complex]]es<ref>[http://eu.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-0471185884.html D. Astruc, Electron Transfer and Radical Processes in Transition-Metal Chemistry, VCH, New York, 1995] (630 pp., preface by [[Henry Taube]]).</ref> and [[Dendrimer|dendritic]] [[molecular]] [[Battery (electricity)|batteries]],<ref>{{cite journal |author1=C. Ornelas |author2=J. Ruiz |author3=C. Belin |author4=D. He is the author of three books, scientific publications and the editor of five books or special issues. He has been a member of the National [[CNRS]] committee from 2000 to 2008 and the President of the Coordination Chemistry Division of the [[French Chemical Society|Société Française de Chimie]] from 2000 to 2004. Didier Astruc is on the Thompson-Reuters list of the top 100 chemists who have achieved the highest citation impact scores for their chemistry papers published between 2000 and 2010,<ref>[http://sciencewatch.com/dr/sci/misc/Top100Chemists2000-10/ sciencewatch link]</ref>  and on the list of the Highest Cited Researchers 2015 and 2016 (Thomson-Reuters),<ref>[http://highlycited.com/ sciencewatch link]</ref> and 2017 to 2023  ([[Clarivate]] Analytics).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://clarivate.com/hcr/2017-researchers-list/|title=Highly Cited Researchers}}</ref>

* Senior Member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] (1995–2005).
* [[Humboldt Award|German-French Humboldt Award]] (Fondation Alexander von Humboldt) (1989).
